Un entrepreneur de Saint-Michel veut con: A Saint-Michel entrepreneur wants to conquer the sports market
Le fondateur d'une entreprise dédié à la: The founder of a company dedicated to muscle recovery won the first edition of the Défi Saint-Michel.
Vendredi dernier j'ai assisté à la prése: Last Friday, I attended the pitch presentations by entrepreneurs who took part in the first edition of the Défi Saint-Michel. We heard about this initiative from Julie, who runs an aesthetics centre and whom we profiled as part of our Hood Heroes series.
C'est finalement le fondateur d'une entr: In the end, the winner was the founder of a company dedicated to muscle recovery, proud to represent Saint-Michel and its entrepreneurial project leaders.
<strong>Au troisième étage du 3737, rue: On the third floor of 3737 Crémazie Street, a first-of-its-kind event took place this Friday, December 20, on the eve of the holiday break. Five entrepreneurs submitted their projects as part of the first edition of the Défi Saint-Michel. The initiative was led by Groupe 3737, an incubator that promotes greater diversity in the business world.
C’est le grand jour ! Comme les enfants: It's the big day! Like children waiting to open their presents, five Saint-Michel entrepreneurs were eagerly awaiting this moment. “This is the end of a six-week journey during which these entrepreneurs worked very, very hard. Today is the big pitch day! The entrepreneurs have five minutes to present their projects,” Maudeleine Myrthil, vice-president of Entrepreneurship at Groupe 3737, explains to the audience.
Quelques soutiens des entrepreneurs se s: A few supporters of the entrepreneurs came out for the occasion. The mayor of the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough, Laurence Lavigne Lalonde, and the MNA for Viau, Frantz Benjamin, are also on hand to witness this initiative, made possible by financial support from the borough and PME MTL, the City of Montréal's business support network.
C’est M. Roland, à la tête d’une entrepr: Mr. Roland, who runs a renovation company, kicks things off. Having grown up in Montréal, he shows understandable nerves, occasionally stumbling over a word but quickly regaining his composure. He doesn't hesitate to give out his phone number to potential clients in the audience. “What sets us apart is that we offer quality renovation work at a price that remains affordable for Saint-Michel residents,” he says. He hopes to win the Défi so he can build his online presence and rent a more comfortable office.
Vient ensuite le tour du Centre communau: Next up is the Centre communautaire La Patience, which provides food and material assistance to neighbourhood residents. Wearing a spotless white shirt and black jacket, Jean Charles Bernard presented the centre's project: moving to a larger space to offer better services to the community.
Puis, le propriétaire de deux restaurant: Then the owner of two restaurants on Saint-Michel Boulevard takes over. His idea? “Many children go to school without eating. This grant would allow me to provide lunch boxes to some of them. I want to do this to give back a little of what comes in to the community,” says Paul Fablon.
C’est avec une mise en scène travaillée: The fourth entrepreneur begins his pitch with a carefully crafted performance. “This project is quite simply an innovation and a revolution!” declares Mikhaïl N. Ngassa, founder of Kherös Sport. It is a body wash formulated to speed up physical recovery for young and adult athletes alike, using natural ingredients with anti-inflammatory properties.
Ngan Julie Trinh, cofondatrice de Pretty: Ngan Julie Trinh, co-founder of Pretty Little Things Ongles & Spa, closes out the morning of pitches. The young woman is championing a project to bring young women in the neighbourhood who have dropped out of school back into education through nail technician training. “I show them they can earn money by working, and I try to get them to go back to school to train in whatever they want,” explains the businesswoman.
Ngan Julie Trinh, co-founder of Pretty Little Things Ongles & Spa, during her pitch. Photo: Loubna Chlaikhy
Au terme de ces cinq présentations, le j: After the five presentations, the jury withdraws to deliberate. In the end, Mikhaïl N. Ngassa's company Kherös Sport wins the Défi Saint-Michel and the $2,500 prize awarded to the winner. It's a proud moment for the man in his thirties, whose ambitions seem boundless.
Mikhaïl N. Ngassa s’est illustré dans l’: Mikhaïl N. Ngassa stood out in the pitch exercise. Energetic, very well prepared and visibly at ease, he presented his product as if it were a star! To the audience's applause, the Kherös Sport body wash was displayed on a stand by an assistant. “I chose to work with a Quebec laboratory and Quebec suppliers. So it's a 100% local and innovative product,” he notes proudly.
L’entrepreneur n’en est pas à son coup d: This is not the entrepreneur's first attempt. He already won third prize at the Gala de Reconnaissance des Entrepreneurs Noirs du Québec last April. Saying he works an average of 85 hours a week, he is determined to make his place and “represent his hood.”
Né en France, il a passé sa jeunesse ent: Born in France, he spent his youth between his parents' Cameroon, France and the United Kingdom. “I played basketball in a training academy when I was young. When I settled in Saint-Michel 15 years ago, the plan then was to go play in the United States, but in the end, it didn't work out,” Mikhail recounts.
Désireux de ne pas abandonner totalement: Wanting to avoid abandoning his passion entirely, he pursued university studies in marketing, communications and public relations. “I always wanted to start a business, but I wanted to combine it with my passion for sports. I spent a year on research and development thanks to government assistance that no longer exists, but which gave me an income during that period,” he explains.
À la fin de cette année d’exploration, i: By the end of that year of exploration, he had his product. In the second year, he launched a first production run of nearly 800 bottles and handed out samples to test his muscle recovery body wash.
<strong>« Je suis le premier chef d’entr: “I'm the first Black business owner in the sports industry in Quebec”
Les quartiers comme Saint-Michel, perçus: Neighbourhoods like Saint-Michel, perceived as poor and multicultural, are all too rarely associated with entrepreneurial innovation. Yet more and more racialized people are embarking on this kind of adventure. “Of course, at the beginning, you think it's going to be harder, especially when you don't have a network. Most people like my energy, so it's not too hard for me, even though I'm the first Black business owner in the sports industry in Quebec,” confides the CEO of Kherös Sport.
Selon lui, l’absence de réseau ne peut ê: According to him, the lack of a network can only be made up for with a lot of work. “When I see people who don't even have LinkedIn or think they can do everything from home, that doesn't work. I go to a huge number of events and meetings, which I choose based on how relevant they are to my field, which is sports. You have to identify the right people, build connections, and so on,” he says.
Mikhaïl N. Ngassa lors de son pitch. Pho: Mikhaïl N. Ngassa during his pitch. Photo: Loubna Chlaikhy
Une méthode qui fonctionne puisque ce tr: It's a method that works, since this hard worker is already starting to make a name for himself. “MNA Frantz Benjamin, who was here earlier, uses my body wash,” Mikail says with pride.
Au total, il a dépensé 20 000 $, puisés: In total, he spent $20,000, taken directly from his savings. It's a risk he doesn't regret taking, because the first test run sold out entirely. Mikhail is now thinking bigger: “The next step is to bring in an investor and launch production. Then I'm already working on new Kherös Sport products, including a body wash for swimmers, for example, a moisturizer, a shampoo… I have a lot of product ideas related to athletic recovery.”
Ses articles étant déjà commercialisés e: With his products already sold online and in a few Montréal shops, he plans to work with distributors to conquer the Quebec market, then the Canadian one. And he won't forget Saint-Michel in his growth plans. “I'd like to offer young people in the neighbourhood missions on social media, for example, get them involved in this project,” he says.
D’une nature ambitieuse, il voit déjà le: Ambitious by nature, he already sees his brand's products being exported around the world.
